resources.string: Lets Paydos see which app is on screen while a session is active, and redirect back when a not-allowed app is opened. It does not read screen content.
Pick a duration, choose which apps are allowed, hand the phone to your child.
One tap on the button below is enough - I\'ll open the rest in order, you just tap \"Allow\"/\"Turn on\" on each screen.
Enter a new PIN to change it
You\'ll need this PIN to end the lock before time is up. Pick something your child doesn\'t know.

If you forget your PIN, this unlocks it instead. Pick something easy for you to remember but that your child wouldn\'t know or guess — not their birth year or name. For example: your first pet\'s name, your favorite teacher\'s last name, or the city you finished high school in.
Enter a new one to change it (optional)
That answer isn\'t right, try again
No recovery answer was set up for this lock
Set a recovery answer too, so you can unlock if you forget your PIN
Forgot both the PIN and the recovery answer? Turning the phone off and back on removes the lock.

Find and open \"Paydos\" on the screen that opens
Needed so Paydos can\'t be easily removed while a session is locked.
This sort option needs Android\'s \"Usage access\" permission. On the screen that opens, find \"Paydos\" in the list and allow it.
Paydos needs a few permissions to work

Without these, the lock feature won't work:

• Accessibility — to see which app is open
• Device Admin — to make it harder to remove the app while locked
• Notifications — to tell you how much time is left

None of them read your screen or collect data.
Turn on the permissions above first
Set a PIN with at least 4 digits
The new PIN must have at least 4 digits
Paydos needs Android\'s Accessibility permission to work while a lock session is active. Before you continue, here\'s exactly what it\'s for:
🔍 What it does: while the lock is active, it checks which app is open on screen.
↩️ Why it\'s needed: if a not-allowed app is opened, it automatically sends you back to the lock screen.
🔒 What it doesn\'t do: it doesn\'t read on-screen text, passwords, or any other content, and no data ever leaves your phone.
⚠️ Heads up: on the next screen, Android may show a red \"Danger\" warning. This is a standard system message shown for every app that requests this permission — not something specific to Paydos.
